report:
S00 is down. I used all 10 changes, counting one rollback, and Z1 is still just under its target.

Changes, aimed at Z1 (priority 1) first:
- chg-0001 to 0004: tilt cut from 6 to 4 on S03-B, S06-A, S02-C and S04-B. These are the cells that face the centre and serve Z1. Z1 coverage went from 78.8% to 85.0%.
- chg-0005 to 0008: power raised from 43 to 45 dBm on the same four cells. This is below the 46 dBm limit. Z1 coverage reached 93.8%.
- chg-0009: S03-C tilt 6 to 4. It gave no Z1 gain, lowered throughput slightly and added an alarm, so I rolled it back in chg-0010. S03-C is back at its original tilt.

Results (before to after):
- Z1: 78.8% to 93.8%. This is still under the 95% threshold, so the alarm is active.
- Z3: 94.1% to 97.7%.
- Z2: 100% throughout. Z4: 98.4% to 99.3%.
- Network coverage: 96.3% to 98.7%.
- Alarm thresholds are unchanged.

Watch:
- Z1 coverage alarm, 93.8% against 95%.
- Overloaded cells: S02-C, S04-B, S05-A, S05-B and S06-A are at about 100% load, so Z1 users are probably being blocked on capacity.
- Interference: SINR is poor for 7 users, up from 3. Z1 5th-percentile throughput is only 0.16 Mbps. Total transmit power rose from 359 W to 406 W.
- Next steps if more budget is allowed:
  - Use CIO to move users off S02-C and S04-B onto cells with spare capacity, such as S03-C, S01-A and S01-C.
  - Try small tilt or power changes on the S01 cells.
  - Restore the tilt and power changes once S00 is back.
